urgency.h: Wage Theft Is Bigger Than Every Other Kind of Theft Combined
urgency.sub: A few dollars an hour doesn't sound like much. Multiply it by every shift, every week, for three years — then add the penalties California stacks on top.

cards.p: California lets you recover unpaid wages going back three years — four under the Unfair Competition Law. That "small" shortfall on every check is a very large number by now.

One extra hour of pay for every missed meal break. Another for every missed rest break. Up to 30 days' wages if your final check was late. Penalties for inaccurate pay stubs. It adds up faster than the wages themselves.

cards.t: It's illegal to fire you for asking
cards.p: Retaliation for a wage complaint is a separate violation with its own damages. You're protected — and if they punish you for calling us, your case just got bigger.

value.h: Every Violation Has a Price Tag in California
value.sub: You don't have to prove they were mean. You just have to prove they didn't pay. The Labor Code does the rest.

items.p: Time-and-a-half after 8 hours in a day or 40 in a week — double time after 12. "Salaried" doesn't automatically mean exempt, and "we don't pay overtime here" isn't a policy, it's a violation.
One extra hour of pay for each missed, short, or late meal break — and another hour for each missed rest break. Per day. Going back years.
Pre-shift setup, post-shift cleanup, answering texts at home, bag checks, "just finish this before you clock in" — all compensable. All owed.
Called a contractor but treated like an employee? Called "exempt" but doing hourly work? You may be owed overtime, breaks, expenses, and benefits for the entire period.
Late or short final paycheck? Up to 30 days of wages as a penalty. Inaccurate pay stubs? Penalties per pay period. Plus interest, plus your attorney's fees — paid by them.

faq.q: I'm salaried. Can I still get overtime?
faq.a: Often, yes. A salary alone doesn't make you "exempt." To be exempt in California you generally must earn at least twice the state minimum wage for full-time work AND spend most of your time on genuinely managerial, administrative, or professional duties. Assistant managers who mostly run a register, "coordinators" doing hourly work — these are classic misclassification cases.

faq.q: I signed something saying I'm an independent contractor.
faq.a: Doesn't matter. California's ABC test looks at how you actually work — who controls your hours, whether your work is the company's core business, whether you truly run your own business. A label on a form can't sign away your rights.

faq.q: Can they fire me for filing a wage claim?
faq.a: Retaliating against you for asserting your wage rights is illegal and creates a second, separate claim with its own damages. Everything you tell us is confidential, and your employer will not hear from us until you decide you're ready.
